security_spec.violation_condition: In the FreeBSD kernel, when pointer masking is enabled for U-mode via Ssnpm (through senvcfg.PMM), the kernel's existing raw-register-value bounds checks in copyinout.S and support.S compare user-provided addresses directly against VM_MAXUSER_ADDRESS without applying the pointer-masking ignore transformation first. Tagged user pointers whose raw value exceeds VM_MAXUSER_ADDRESS but whose hardware-transformed effective address falls within the valid user range would be spuriously rejected with EFAULT by the kernel's software bounds check, even though the hardware would have correctly accessed user memory after stripping the tag bits. Conversely, if the kernel attempts to 'compensate' by naively stripping tag bits before the bounds check without verifying the sign-extension invariant mandated by the spec, a crafted pointer whose sign-extended transformation lands in kernel space could bypass the user/kernel boundary check.
security_spec.summary: ZPM pointer masking introduced normative rules for upper-bit ignore transformations that break FreeBSD's raw VM_MAXUSER_ADDRESS bounds-checking in copyinout.S/support.S: tagged U-mode pointers pass through S-mode SUM-based copyin/copyout with S-mode PM settings, so the kernel must either apply the ignore transformation before bounds-checking or accept that tagged pointers are rejected until the kernel explicitly configures and accounts for per-mode PMLEN settings
